tagline.text: A Mindanao tribal culture garden village overlooking Macajalar Bay

location.label: Location
location.text: Malasag Hill, Cugman, Cagayan de Oro City

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱300–1,000 (per person, admission, transport and meals; lodging not included)

children.text: This government-run cultural garden village sits on the Cugman hills, about 30 minutes by car from downtown Cagayan de Oro. You can see traditional houses of Mindanao's indigenous tribes, gardens, walking trails and a viewpoint over Macajalar Bay all in one visit.

The Gardens of Malasag Eco-Tourism Village is a cultural garden on the slopes of a protected watershed forest in Barangay Cugman, Cagayan de Oro City. According to the information sheet from the Tourism Infrastructure and Enterprise Zone Authority (TIEZA), it was conceived in 1992 and inspired by the Gardens of Granada in Spain and Butchart Gardens in Canada. Sources give the site area as anything from 6.2 to 7.2 hectares, but they agree that forest trails connect it to a forest reserve of about 57 hectares.
The heart of the village is the
tribal village

, a cluster of houses of the indigenous tribes of northern Mindanao. TIEZA's material introduces the traditional homes of the Subanon, Talaandig, Higaonon, Tigwahanon, Umayamnon and Pulangihon tribes and says that crafts, rituals and dances are presented here. Flower gardens, an aviary, a small animal area, an open-air theater, a swimming pool and lodging cottages round out the grounds, which makes it a popular day outing.

The view is the village's biggest asset. From the hilltop viewpoint you look down on Macajalar Bay and the Cagayan de Oro coastline, and on a clear day the view stretches far out to sea. It sits higher than downtown, so it is cooler and a good escape from the midday heat. Visitor reviews are mixed, though. The Tripadvisor rating is in the high 3s out of 5; some reviewers praise the views and atmosphere, while others mention aging facilities and a lack of interpretation. Go expecting a modest public cultural garden rather than a flashy theme park and you are more likely to be satisfied.

The facilities listed in the TIEZA material show that this is more than a garden: it is a small multi-purpose tourism complex. It lists a Lantana Learning Center for about 20 people, the Higaonon Resto Café seating about 60, an open-air amphitheater for 200 to 300 people, an air-conditioned function room and a hillside function room, souvenir shops, and picnic sheds with barbecue grills. Lodging is divided into Lantao, deluxe and standard cottages, plus a dormitory for about 70 people. These figures come from the material, so check the actual operating status before you visit. The site is run by a government agency: TIEZA manages it, reportedly through lease or management arrangements with private operators. That is why weddings, seminars, school outings and corporate workshops are often held here. If a group event is on the day you visit, some areas may be crowded or closed off.

You can walk through traditional houses of the indigenous tribes of northern Mindanao, such as the Subanon, Talaandig and Higaonon. Each house differs in architecture and household tools, and on some days you may see weaving or craft-making. TIEZA's material also describes hands-on activities such as weaving, crafts, ornament making and weapon making in the ethnic museum area under the National Museum, but the actual programs may differ from day to day.
This lookout faces Macajalar Bay and the Cagayan de Oro cityscape. It looks best on a clear morning or around sunset, and it is where most visitors linger to take photos.
A short canopy walk and a suspension bridge are included in the admission fee. They are small, but they give you the feeling of walking above the forest, and children enjoy them.

Flower gardens and forest trails run through the village. The walking is light enough for adults and children alike, and in some places signs let you check plant names. The flower shower garden, a collection of rare plants and a center that cares for rescued birds are also sights described in the TIEZA material.

There is an aviary where you can see birds up close and an area with small animals such as rabbits. It is popular with families with children. Please follow staff instructions when feeding the animals.
There is a swimming pool that costs extra, and you can rent a picnic shed with barbecue grills for a family gathering or group picnic. If you plan to swim, be sure to bring a change of clothes.

Some reviewers say tribal dance shows are held at the open-air theater, and several sources mention a start time of around 4 PM. However, reviewers say the shows are not on a fixed daily schedule, so it is best to confirm before you go.
The village has cottages, a dormitory for groups and a campground, so you can stay overnight and enjoy the hilltop night air. It is also often used for seminars and group events.

items.title: Half-day route
items.subtitle: An afternoon visit with a show and the view

children.text: Set out from downtown Cagayan de Oro. A taxi or Grab is the easiest, and the drive takes about
30 minutes
Pay the admission fee at the entrance and follow the garden trail to visit the tribal houses one by one. Taking your time with the displays and crafts inside takes about
1 hour
. Each tribe's houses differ in shape and decoration, so it is fun to compare them as you read the name signs.
Cross the canopy walk and the hanging bridge, then visit the aviary and the small animal area.
Ask the staff whether a tribal show is being held at the open-air theater, and if so, find a seat.
Head up to the viewdeck and watch the sun set over Macajalar Bay.
Take a taxi back downtown before it gets dark. Arrange your ride back in advance.
Because it is in the hills, it gets dark quickly after sunset and rides become scarce. If you came by public transport, it is safer to head down before dark.
Check in and drop your bags at the cottage. Be sure to confirm the room rate and what is included before booking.
Look around the gardens, the tribal village and the canopy walk.
Watch the sunset from the viewdeck and have dinner at a restaurant in the village.
Relax at the pool or by a campfire (extra charge).
The next morning, walk the trails in the mist and cool air, then check out.
There are direct flights from Manila (NAIA) to Laguindingan Airport (CGY) in Cagayan de Oro. The flight takes about
1 hour 30 minutes
There are also routes into CGY from Cebu. Check airline announcements for the schedule.

items.title: From the airport to downtown Cagayan de Oro

children.text: Laguindingan Airport is far from downtown, and the trip by bus, airport van or taxi takes about
1 hour
One option is to take a bus or van from the airport to the downtown bus terminal and transfer from there to a vehicle heading toward Cugman.
A taxi straight from the airport to Malasag can cost much more. Confirm whether the meter is used and roughly what the fare will be before you leave.
It is about
30 minutes
from downtown by taxi or Grab. Taking a motorcycle taxi up is also common.
One suggested route is to ride a jeepney toward Cugman (the RD-Cugman or RD-Gusa routes), get off at the Malasag crossing and take a motorcycle taxi. Routes and fares change, so check locally.
If you are driving or have a rental car, enter "Gardens of Malasag Eco-Tourism Village" into Waze or Google Maps; parking is available.
It can be hard to find a taxi back, so you could also arrange waiting or return-pickup times with the driver who brought you.
The dry season from December to May is best for walking and enjoying the view. On clear days the view opens up all the way to Macajalar Bay and the trails are not slippery.
In the rainy season, mist and cloud can blur the view, and the dirt paths can be slippery when it rains. During the day, the morning or the hour around sunset is the coolest.

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary depending on local conditions.
The village has standard and deluxe cottages and a dormitory for groups. The operator's rate sheet lists cottages at about
per night, while another article lists
. Rates change with the season, so ask before you book. Many sources say only cash is accepted, so ask in advance how reservations and payment work.

The simplest option for meals is the restaurant or café in the village. Menus and opening hours vary by season, so it helps to bring a few snacks and water. If you do not want to stay overnight, the most common plan is to book a hotel downtown and make this a half-day visit. For downtown hotels and restaurants, see the
Cagayan de Oro
entry.

Seminar packages are available for groups. According to an article, the overnight packages, which have a minimum group size, include meals, a function room and pool use. If you have a large group, contact the village directly for a quote.
According to the operator, only cash payments are accepted. Bring plenty of cash for admission, the pool and food.
Opening hours differ by source. Some say 6 AM to 10 PM, while others say it is open 24 hours, so check by phone (+63 917 136 3060) or the official Facebook page before you go.
Reviewers mention a tribal show at around 4 PM, but it does not appear to be on a fixed schedule. If you want to see it, ask in advance.
If you want to swim, bring swimwear, a change of clothes and a towel.
In the hills it is cooler than downtown and it sometimes rains. A light jacket and an umbrella or raincoat are helpful.
Decide your ride back before you enter. After dark, taxis and motorcycle taxis become scarce.
Put trash in the designated places, and do not pick the plants or touch the animals. Follow staff instructions.
Some stretches have little shade, so bring a hat, sunscreen and water.
You can buy tribal crafts at the souvenir shops. Check prices locally, and ask the staff which tribe an item comes from before you buy to hear its story.
Facilities and operating schedules can change a lot from time to time, so be sure to check before you visit.
Some reviewers say the facilities are aging or that the animal areas are quiet. Keep your expectations realistic.
Rates and opening hours change often. Check the latest announcements.
After dark the mountain road is dim and rides are scarce.
After rain the dirt paths and bridges can be slippery, so wear non-slip shoes.
Follow the on-site staff's guidance on the safety of the trails and canopy walk, and keep children close.
It is about
30 minutes
away by car. Hotels, malls and restaurants are clustered there, so it is a good place for dinner after your visit.
A highland attraction on the way up toward Bukidnon. It is a separate day trip, and you should check the travel time locally.
A volcanic island reached by land east of Cagayan de Oro to the port of Balingoan, then by ferry. Plan it as a separate trip of at least one night.
